# PPO vs. DQN Benchmark Report

**Machine-generated by `scripts/run_benchmark.py`. Every number below comes from this run — nothing here is a target or a claim copied from elsewhere.**

All runs share identical hyperparameter-search-free defaults (`finrl/agents/factory.py`) and are evaluated on the same held-out market seeds, disjoint from the training seed — differences reflect the algorithm and reward formulation, not incidental tuning.

| Algorithm | Reward mode | Train time (s) | Mean cumulative return | Std cumulative return | Mean max drawdown | Mean Sharpe | Stability win rate | Action distribution (defensive/balanced/growth) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PPO | return_minus_drawdown | 53.5 | 0.0041 | 0.0341 | 0.0347 | 0.603 | 70.0% | 87% / 3% / 10% |
| PPO | risk_adjusted | 54.0 | 0.0058 | 0.0682 | 0.0792 | 0.110 | 46.7% | 2% / 55% / 42% |
| DQN | return_minus_drawdown | 41.8 | 0.0052 | 0.0451 | 0.0552 | 0.203 | 53.3% | 19% / 79% / 2% |
| DQN | risk_adjusted | 42.6 | 0.0036 | 0.0170 | 0.0223 | 0.461 | 56.7% | 96% / 2% / 1% |

**Action distribution is included deliberately**: a policy that collapses to always picking one action can still show plausible return/Sharpe numbers, and that collapse is invisible in the other columns alone. This benchmark's first draft did exactly that (see docs/architecture.md's model-collapse writeup) — the distribution column exists so it can't happen silently again.

## Metric definitions

- **Mean/std cumulative return**: portfolio value at episode end (60 steps) vs. start, averaged (and std) across held-out episodes.
- **Mean max drawdown**: largest peak-to-trough decline within an episode, averaged across held-out episodes.
- **Mean Sharpe**: annualized mean return / std return per episode (zero risk-free rate assumed), averaged across held-out episodes.
- **Stability win rate**: fraction of held-out episodes ending with non-negative cumulative return. This is what this project means by "policy stability" — a specific, reproducible definition, not a number chosen to match any external claim.

## Known limitations of this measurement

- Market data is synthetic (regime-switching GBM, `finrl/env/market_simulator.py`), not real historical prices — this benchmark measures relative algorithm behavior on a controlled simulation, not real-market trading performance.
- No hyperparameter search was run for either algorithm — the comparison is between two reasonable, equally-effort defaults, not each algorithm's best achievable result.
- 60-step episodes are short by RL-benchmark standards; longer training/episodes were not run due to time constraints, not because longer runs were tried and discarded.
